name: Citizenship for Descendants of Czechoslovak Citizens Born in Slovak Territory (3rd-Generation Descent)

qualifying_event.description: A person whose parent, grandparent, or great-grandparent was a Czechoslovak state citizen born in the territory of present-day Slovakia (i.e. Czechoslovakia existed 1918-1992/93) may apply for Slovak citizenship. As of a 15 July 2026 amendment, applicants no longer need to hold or obtain a Slovak residence permit to apply -- eligibility now rests solely on documented ancestry.
qualifying_event.evidence_hint: Documentation proving the qualifying ancestor's Czechoslovak citizenship and birth in present-day Slovak territory -- civil-status records, naturalization records, ship manifests, or similar historical documents; the July 2026 amendment explicitly allows multiple supporting document types rather than a single definitive record.

requirements.blocker_text: At least one parent, grandparent, or great-grandparent was a Czechoslovak state citizen born in the territory of present-day Slovakia.
Documentary proof that the qualifying ancestor was a Czechoslovak citizen born in present-day Slovak territory (multiple supporting-document types accepted per the July 2026 amendment).

evidence_required.document: Proof of ancestor's Czechoslovak citizenship and birth in present-day Slovak territory (civil-status records, naturalization records, ship manifests, or equivalent)
Chain-of-descent documentation linking applicant to the qualifying ancestor

outcome.physical_presence_requirement: as of the 15 July 2026 amendment, no Slovak residence permit or residency requirement applies to this route

sources.title: Slov-Lex (Slovak Republic's official legislative/gazette portal) -- Law 72/2022 Z.z., amending the Act on State Citizenship, effective 1 April 2022: introduced Section 7(2)(j), citizenship eligibility for descendants (parent, grandparent, or great-grandparent) of a Czechoslovak citizen born on Slovak territory; ORIGINALLY required 5 years' continuous residence in Slovakia (with exemptions for under-14s, former Czech citizens, diaspora-certificate holders, over-65s, and those passing a Slovak language exam) -- this residence requirement was REMOVED by a later 2026 amendment, see akmv_2026_amendment

AKMV (Slovak immigration law firm) -- amendment to the Act on State Citizenship, in force from 15 July 2026: abolishes the residence-permit requirement for the 2022 Czechoslovak-descent route entirely, clarifies acceptable evidence types (multiple supporting documents, not one definitive record), introduces electronic citizenship certificates (valid 90 days to apply for a passport per this source; a separate secondary source states 6 months), and transfers foreign-citizenship-acquisition recording duties from the national Ministry of Interior to regional district offices

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Slovakia). STATUS: DRAFT. THIS IS THE SINGLE MOST SIGNIFICANT AND TIME-SENSITIVE FINDING IN THIS BUILD. Slovakia's 2022 law (Zakon 72/2022, tier-1 slov-lex.sk confirmed) opened citizenship to descendants of ANY former Czechoslovak citizen born in present-day Slovak territory, going back to a GREAT-GRANDPARENT (three generations) -- explicitly estimated by press coverage at the time to reach roughly 700,000-800,000 people worldwide, concentrated in US Czech/Slovak-American communities (Ohio, Pennsylvania, New York, West Virginia). A FURTHER amendment took effect 15 JULY 2026 -- SEVEN WEEKS before this build -- that REMOVED the residence-permit requirement entirely, making this now a pure documented-ancestry route with NO Slovak residence obligation at all, structurally now closer to Israel's Law of Return or Romania's Article 11 than to a conventional descent-with-residence naturalisation track. SOURCING CAVEAT, IMPORTANT: the tier-1 slov-lex.sk source confirms the 2022 law's ORIGINAL text (which DID include a 5-year residence requirement with exemptions) -- this dataset could NOT independently locate the specific slov-lex.sk statutory text for the July 2026 amendment itself in this pass, despite searching; the amendment's existence and substance rest on a tier-3 law firm source (AKMV) corroborated by a tier-4 press aggregator report of a Ministry of Interior statement (not independently used as a formal source here, but consistent). This file is kept DRAFT specifically because the CURRENT, OPERATIVE version of the rule (no-residence-requirement) is not yet confirmed at tier-1 -- the tier-1 source on file describes the SUPERSEDED 2022 rules.
